01 · Why

Answers don't teach.

"What I cannot create, I do not understand. What I do not understand, I cannot create. What I cannot create or understand, I cannot teach."

After Feynman. It's the site's rule, not a poster.

An answer ends the interaction. A guide stays.

Chatbots hand over an answer and move on — cognitive offloading dressed as help. Every route here ends at a blank page you fill yourself.

Proof is a working build, not a quiz score.

You explain it on camera, you code the real kernel, you rebuild it days later from nothing. The ladder is understand → create → teach.

Label everything: live, in build, designed.

No demo theater. Every claim on this page carries its status.

The field is a terrain map: elevation is significance, search is by meaning, and Directions draws prerequisite-correct routes across it. Every lesson has eight ways in — read, listen, solve, write, teach on camera, present to a live coach, collaborate, share. Spaced-recall decks run on 540 lessons. A research feed tracks ~25k items and publishes The Daily Delve, a daily edition with an audio brief.

actual product — the map, routing ML Maths → Generative Models

And the part most platforms skip: learning by building. Voice-led Studio sessions where you predict, then write the real code — CS231n rebuilt in-browser, every gradient yours, every run checked exactly.

03 · The agentic layer in build

One ask becomes a route

Next: a planner you can read — it parses the ask, walks the graph, places create gates, and drafts the lessons the catalog is missing. The feed already knows the gaps; the generation pipeline exists; everything lands in a review queue. Nothing auto-ships.

The platform is also built agentically — 25 codified agent pipelines make the content, agent fleets review it, the daily edition publishes itself.
